hushgram.title: v0.0.8
hushgram.body:
HushGram v0.0.8 has 79 patches for Instagram 450.0.0.50.77, 1 more than v0.0.7. All seven builds of that version patch, and it needs Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer on Android 9 and newer. Here's everything that changed.

## What's new

* New patch: Hide suggested accounts in DMs takes the Accounts to follow section off the bottom of your messages (#112).
* With Hide suggested posts on, Home no longer sits on gray loading boxes after you switch to an account that follows nobody (#104, #105).
* View stories anonymously has a new switch, Gray out stories you've watched (#113).
* Sanitize sharing links takes off the share id Instagram began adding to copied post, reel and profile links (#109).
* Hide the Stories tray keeps the floating tray away when you come back to Home (#88).
* Simple mode in Morphe Manager picks 75 of the 79 patches now, and every description says where its switch is.
* Opening HushGram settings from the launcher shortcut no longer crashes Instagram while it restarts its screen.

## Instagram

* HushGram 0.0.8 adds 1 patch, for 79 in all, and stays on Instagram 450.0.0.50.77 with Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer. All seven builds of that version patch: the arm64 ones (385611395, 385611400, 385611404, 385611431 and 385611438) and the x86 and x86_64 ones (385611439 and 385611440).
* New patch, Hide suggested accounts in DMs. Turn on its switch under Messages and restart Instagram, and the Accounts to follow section at the bottom of your messages isn't built. Your chats and follow requests stay, and so does a section of people who follow you. It's in the default selection with its switch off. Asked for in #112.
* Copy the commenter's username only shows up in HushGram settings when Copy username actually went into your build. On an Instagram build where it couldn't, Copy comment still works, the extra switch stays out of the way, and the diagnostic report says why.
* With Hide the Stories tray on, the tray could still show up at the top of Home for a few seconds after you watched a story you opened in DMs. When you come back to Home partway down the feed, Instagram floats a copy of the tray over it, and that copy now stays hidden too. Reported in #88.
* Disable analytics is stricter about which saved address it treats as the crash reporter's. It only follows the address when it's saved right after it's built, so a later Instagram build that saves something else there won't have that value changed. Both places Instagram 450 saves it still qualify.
* Disable analytics won't apply to an Instagram build where it finds none of the addresses reports are sent to, even if it finds the contacts and location setup screens or Instagram's live event stream. Skipping those screens protects nothing by itself, and turning the stream off only moves events to the regular upload. When a build has only some of what Disable analytics or Sanitize sharing links work on, the switch's description in HushGram settings now says how many it covers.
* Opening HushGram's settings from the launcher shortcut while Instagram was restarting its screen could crash Instagram, because the screen still had Instagram's startup look and couldn't draw text yet. The settings now wait until the screen is ready and then open.
* View stories anonymously has a new switch, Gray out stories you've watched. It starts off, so a story you watch keeps its colored ring as it does now. Turn it on and a watched story turns gray and moves to the end of the row on your phone, while Instagram still isn't told you watched it. Asked for in #113 and on #92.
* Sanitize sharing links now also cleans a link that's copied to the clipboard as a link item rather than as text, which kept its share id before. Thanks to @Aholicknight, who spotted it and sent the approach in #107.
* With Hide suggested posts on, Home no longer sits on gray loading boxes after you switch to an account whose Home is all suggestions, such as a new account that follows nobody. Home used to remember every post it had kept since Instagram started, so the first account's posts kept it from ending. Now only Home's latest load counts. Reported in #104 and #105.
* Messages and notices are plainer too. Import and export results, save progress, the sign-in notice and the Developer page now say what happened and what to do next, without terms like "flag" or "cache". All six languages were updated.
* The rows in HushGram settings now explain themselves in plain English. Each summary says what you'll notice and, where it matters, to restart Instagram to see the change. The German, Spanish, Indonesian, Brazilian Portuguese, Turkish and Korean text was updated to match.
* Every patch description in Morphe Manager is rewritten in plain English. Each one says what changes, why you might want it, and ends with where its switch is, or that it works with no switch.
* Morphe Manager's simple mode now picks 75 of the 79 patches, so you don't need Expert mode to get a feature. Every patch with a switch in HushGram settings is in, and one that comes in this way changes nothing until you turn its switch on. The 25 that joined are Clean up Reels, Don't send reel watch history, Download any video, Hide group buttons on the share sheet, Hide Reels in the feed, Hide suggested accounts in Reels, Hide suggested people on profiles, Hide that you're typing, Hide the Explore grid, Hide the Reels tab, Hide the Repost button, Keep a seek bar on Reels, Keep Reels auto scroll on, Loop a story, Read messages without the seen receipt, Remove the empty space at the bottom, See who a story mentions, Show a post's exact time, Show a story's exact time, Spoof location, Start Home on Following, Stop Story auto-advance, Tap to play, Turn off double tap to like and View stories anonymously. Change version code, Open developer options, Pure black dark mode and View DM photos and videos anonymously stay out, and the README says why.
* Coming from an earlier build, 24 switches start off now where they used to start on once you picked their patch. Under Feed, Start Home on Following and Show a post's exact time. Under Explore, Hide the Explore grid. Under Reels, Hide Reels in the feed, Hide suggested accounts, Hide the Follow button, Hide creation and promotion pills, Hide friends' activity and comment previews, Don't send reel watch history, Turn off double tap to like, Hide the Reels tab, Keep a seek bar and Keep auto scroll on. Under Stories, Stop Story auto-advance, Loop a story, Show a story's exact time, See who a story mentions and View stories anonymously. Under Playback, Tap to play. Under Sharing, Hide group buttons and Hide the Repost button. Under Profiles, Hide suggested people. Under Layout, Remove the empty space at the bottom. Under Downloads, Download feed videos. If you used one and never changed its switch, turn it on again in HushGram settings, or import a settings backup you exported before updating. A switch you'd set yourself keeps your choice.
* Each patch's description in Morphe Manager now says where its switch is in HushGram settings and whether it starts on or off, and the install steps end with opening HushGram settings to turn on what you want.
* Expert mode groups the patches under 15 headings instead of 8, so Interface no longer holds 43 of them. The new ones are Ghost mode, Messages, Stories, Reels, Playback, Interaction and Profiles, and most match a section in HushGram settings.
* Download any story now also looks at the type a story was posted as before it picks the menu's rows, the way Instagram's own story viewer tells a photo story with music from a filmed video. Instagram sends most photo stories with music as a video, and only some of them carry the flag the menu checked until now, so the rest got a single Download that saved the video. A story posted as a photo that arrives as a video gets Download as video and Download as photo. Plain photo and video stories keep their one Download, and the diagnostic report counts which kind of story each menu was for. Reported in #98.
* Sanitize sharing links now also takes off the share id Instagram began adding to copied post, reel and profile links under a different short name each time, such as ?obrf= or ?mdxt=. Every other part of the link stays as Instagram wrote it.
* README's Troubleshooting has a section for an Instagram that feels slow right after a Root Mount install. Android's compiled copy of the app was made from Meta's code, so it's thrown out and Instagram runs uncompiled until it's compiled again, and the section gives the root shell command that does it straight away.

## Tooling

* The patch contract check can count a name Instagram asks its shared string pool for, on the rules marked for it. Some 450 builds (385611395, 400, 439 and 440) ask the pool for a few names that 438 loads itself, so the check turned down the story link parser, the setup screen presenter and the share sheet's target list there even with the patch in the right place. Other rules still count only names a method loads itself, so a pool ask elsewhere can't confuse them.
* Release notes now have to open with a short What's new list of 5 to 8 one-line bullets, with the full list of changes under it. The notes builder won't write them without one, or with one that's grown too long to scan. Asked for in #86 and #106.
* Hide ads has tests of its own. One checks that only an on switch with HushGram ready and not paused hides an ad. The other checks that each supported Instagram build has exactly one place where ads go into a feed, and that HushGram's check is the first thing that runs there.
* The Instagram internals reference now includes measured network traffic, background activity and unplugged battery discharge, with exact installed-build evidence and the limits of each measurement. The observation uses an installation reporting HushGram 0.0.5 and does not establish savings against stock or validate the current release.
* The push gate, the release receipt, the dependency audit and the all-patches check wait their turn in the machine's build queue now, when it has one, instead of starting Gradle or the patcher straight away. The gate holds one slot from its first build to its last patch run, and a push made with `HUSHGRAM_ALLOW_RELEASE=1` goes ahead of everyday builds in the line. `BUILD_QUEUE_SCRIPT` names the queue and `HUSHGRAM_BUILD_WRAPPER` the script that runs Gradle. Without them the scripts run as they did before and say so.
* The push gate runs its quick checks first. The catalog, both lints and the runtime tests go in one build, and the patch tests (most of a quarter hour) and the bundle come after it, so a lint slip or a stale catalog stops the push in a few minutes. A declared build with no fixture stops it before anything is built.
* The push gate keeps its results when it removes its worktree, pass or fail. The test results, the bundle and its SBOM, each declared build's patch reports and its passing patch run go in a folder named for the commit, under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HushGram\gate` unless `HUSHGRAM_GATE_CACHE` names another place, with a manifest of what the gate ran and how far it got. The newest three are kept. Before, a gate's test results went with its worktree, and the release check had to run the patch tests again.
* `build-release-receipt.ps1 -FromGate` and `validate-release-facts.ps1 -FromGate` read the gate's run of the commit they check instead of doing its work again. The receipt takes the gate's bundle and SBOM when none was built here, and reads each declared build's patch run back when the gate made it with the same bundle, catalog, desktop CLI and APK. The release check takes the gate's test results, bundle and receipt when the checkout has none, and the index push passes `-FromGate` by itself. A run is read only when its manifest, tree, hashes and test counts still hold up for that commit, and every check runs on what's read. Anything else and the scripts build, test and patch as before.
* The index push that follows a release doesn't build and test the release's sources all over again. When every file it pushes is an index file and the only lines changed since a commit the gate passed are the index, the README's latest release sentence and the bug form's version, the gate is skipped. The release switch, the commit checks, the suites and the release check against the published release still run. The gate runs anyway when the kept run doesn't hold up, or when it would patch a build here that the kept run didn't patch with the same fixture and desktop CLI.
* The gate's kept run is held to more before a push or a release leans on it. An index push is gated in full when the fixture folder has changed since the gate ran, since a build added or replaced there changes what the patch tests read. The same goes when `pre-push.ps1` or `gate-evidence.ps1` changed after the run was made, or when a kept patched APK, patch report or merge no longer matches what the gate stamped. Two gates of one commit no longer write into the same folder. The second one stops until the first is done. Pruning still keeps the newest three runs, and failed runs go before passed ones, so a release's passed run survives a busy day of pushes.
* When the fixture folder holds more than one copy of the Instagram version the bundle declares, the gate patches the declared build, picked by its version code. It used to take whichever file sorted first, so a second full bundle kept beside the declared one sent the patch step to the wrong build.
* `scripts/release/` holds the helpers a release used to need by hand. `preflight.ps1` runs the quick checks in a few minutes before the source push (a clean checkout on main, every declared build in the fixture folder, the desktop CLI, the release facts, the CHANGELOG section and the patch tests that read no Instagram build) and says how long each took. `patch-all-builds.ps1` patches every Instagram build in the fixture folder with the whole catalog and reports the patches each applied and missed and the CLI's warnings, patching a build kept as a bundle from the bundle rather than its base split, and reading the gate's run back with `-FromGate`. `release_notes.py` builds the GitHub notes from a CHANGELOG section with every bullet in it, and `count_tests.py` counts the test results, the gate's included, and prints the index description's validation sentence. The release steps in CONTRIBUTING.md use all four.
* A push that changes a PowerShell script has every tracked script parsed before anything else runs, and a script that doesn't parse stops the push. Most of them run only for a release or with a phone, so a slip such as a variable name run into a colon used to surface there first.

## Install or update

* Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer is still all you need.
* Update the HushGram source in Morphe Manager, or add it with the link in the README.
* Coming from 0.0.7, 24 switches start off now where they used to start on. If something you used seems gone after the update, turn its switch back on in HushGram settings.
* Instagram 450.0.0.50.77 is still the target. Build 385611438, the (480-640dpi) bundle on APKMirror, is the one every check runs on. The other arm64 builds (385611395, 385611400, 385611404, 385611431) and the x86 and x86_64 ones (385611439, 385611440) patch too, but Manager still names only 385611438, so it shows the others as unsupported. The .mpp is a patch bundle, not an Instagram APK.
* Keep the manager's signing key for updates, so the new build installs over the old one and you stay signed in.
* Read Before you sign in in the README first. A spare account keeps your main one out of it.

## Validation

2925 runtime tests and all 1213 patch tests passed locally. All 79 patches applied to Instagram 450.0.0.50.77 build 385611438 without forcing, and the resource and injected-code checks passed. The other six builds of 450.0.0.50.77 took all 79 patches too. The receipt and SHA256SUMS.txt beside the bundle list every file's hash.

* With Hide the Stories tray on, the tray could still show up at the top of Home for a few seconds after you watched a story you opened in DMs. When you come back to Home partway down the feed, Instagram floats a copy of the tray over it, and that copy now stays hidden too. Reported in #88.
* Disable analytics is stricter about which saved address it treats as the crash reporter's. It only follows the address when it's saved right after it's built, so a later Instagram build that saves something else there won't have that value changed. Both places Instagram 450 saves it still qualify.
* Disable analytics won't apply to an Instagram build where it finds none of the addresses reports are sent to, even if it finds the contacts and location setup screens or Instagram's live event stream. Skipping those screens protects nothing by itself, and turning the stream off only moves events to the regular upload. When a build has only some of what Disable analytics or Sanitize sharing links work on, the switch's description in HushGram settings now says how many it covers.
* Opening HushGram's settings from the launcher shortcut while Instagram was restarting its screen could crash Instagram, because the screen still had Instagram's startup look and couldn't draw text yet. The settings now wait until the screen is ready and then open.
* View stories anonymously has a new switch, Gray out stories you've watched. It starts off, so a story you watch keeps its colored ring as it does now. Turn it on and a watched story turns gray and moves to the end of the row on your phone, while Instagram still isn't told you watched it. Asked for in #113 and on #92.
* Sanitize sharing links now also cleans a link that's copied to the clipboard as a link item rather than as text, which kept its share id before. Thanks to @Aholicknight, who spotted it and sent the approach in #107.
* With Hide suggested posts on, Home no longer sits on gray loading boxes after you switch to an account whose Home is all suggestions, such as a new account that follows nobody. Home used to remember every post it had kept since Instagram started, so the first account's posts kept it from ending. Now only Home's latest load counts. Reported in #104 and #105.
* Messages and notices are plainer too. Import and export results, save progress, the sign-in notice and the Developer page now say what happened and what to do next, without terms like "flag" or "cache". All six languages were updated.
* The rows in HushGram settings now explain themselves in plain English. Each summary says what you'll notice and, where it matters, to restart Instagram to see the change. The German, Spanish, Indonesian, Brazilian Portuguese, Turkish and Korean text was updated to match.
* Every patch description in Morphe Manager is rewritten in plain English. Each one says what changes, why you might want it, and ends with where its switch is, or that it works with no switch.
* Morphe Manager's simple mode now picks 75 of the 79 patches, so you don't need Expert mode to get a feature. Every patch with a switch in HushGram settings is in, and one that comes in this way changes nothing until you turn its switch on. The 25 that joined are Clean up Reels, Don't send reel watch history, Download any video, Hide group buttons on the share sheet, Hide Reels in the feed, Hide suggested accounts in Reels, Hide suggested people on profiles, Hide that you're typing, Hide the Explore grid, Hide the Reels tab, Hide the Repost button, Keep a seek bar on Reels, Keep Reels auto scroll on, Loop a story, Read messages without the seen receipt, Remove the empty space at the bottom, See who a story mentions, Show a post's exact time, Show a story's exact time, Spoof location, Start Home on Following, Stop Story auto-advance, Tap to play, Turn off double tap to like and View stories anonymously. Change version code, Open developer options, Pure black dark mode and View DM photos and videos anonymously stay out, and the README says why.
* Coming from an earlier build, 24 switches start off now where they used to start on once you picked their patch. Under Feed, Start Home on Following and Show a post's exact time. Under Explore, Hide the Explore grid. Under Reels, Hide Reels in the feed, Hide suggested accounts, Hide the Follow button, Hide creation and promotion pills, Hide friends' activity and comment previews, Don't send reel watch history, Turn off double tap to like, Hide the Reels tab, Keep a seek bar and Keep auto scroll on. Under Stories, Stop Story auto-advance, Loop a story, Show a story's exact time, See who a story mentions and View stories anonymously. Under Playback, Tap to play. Under Sharing, Hide group buttons and Hide the Repost button. Under Profiles, Hide suggested people. Under Layout, Remove the empty space at the bottom. Under Downloads, Download feed videos. If you used one and never changed its switch, turn it on again in HushGram settings, or import a settings backup you exported before updating. A switch you'd set yourself keeps your choice.
* Each patch's description in Morphe Manager now says where its switch is in HushGram settings and whether it starts on or off, and the install steps end with opening HushGram settings to turn on what you want.
* Expert mode groups the patches under 15 headings instead of 8, so Interface no longer holds 43 of them. The new ones are Ghost mode, Messages, Stories, Reels, Playback, Interaction and Profiles, and most match a section in HushGram settings.
* Download any story now also looks at the type a story was posted as before it picks the menu's rows, the way Instagram's own story viewer tells a photo story with music from a filmed video. Instagram sends most photo stories with music as a video, and only some of them carry the flag the menu checked until now, so the rest got a single Download that saved the video. A story posted as a photo that arrives as a video gets Download as video and Download as photo. Plain photo and video stories keep their one Download, and the diagnostic report counts which kind of story each menu was for. Reported in #98.
* Sanitize sharing links now also takes off the share id Instagram began adding to copied post, reel and profile links under a different short name each time, such as ?obrf= or ?mdxt=. Every other part of the link stays as Instagram wrote it.
* README's Troubleshooting has a section for an Instagram that feels slow right after a Root Mount install. Android's compiled copy of the app was made from Meta's code, so it's thrown out and Instagram runs uncompiled until it's compiled again, and the section gives the root shell command that does it straight away.

## Tooling

* The patch contract check can count a name Instagram asks its shared string pool for, on the rules marked for it. Some 450 builds (385611395, 400, 439 and 440) ask the pool for a few names that 438 loads itself, so the check turned down the story link parser, the setup screen presenter and the share sheet's target list there even with the patch in the right place. Other rules still count only names a method loads itself, so a pool ask elsewhere can't confuse them.
* Release notes now have to open with a short What's new list of 5 to 8 one-line bullets, with the full list of changes under it. The notes builder won't write them without one, or with one that's grown too long to scan. Asked for in #86 and #106.
* Hide ads has tests of its own. One checks that only an on switch with HushGram ready and not paused hides an ad. The other checks that each supported Instagram build has exactly one place where ads go into a feed, and that HushGram's check is the first thing that runs there.
* The Instagram internals reference now includes measured network traffic, background activity and unplugged battery discharge, with exact installed-build evidence and the limits of each measurement. The observation uses an installation reporting HushGram 0.0.5 and does not establish savings against stock or validate the current release.
* The push gate, the release receipt, the dependency audit and the all-patches check wait their turn in the machine's build queue now, when it has one, instead of starting Gradle or the patcher straight away. The gate holds one slot from its first build to its last patch run, and a push made with `HUSHGRAM_ALLOW_RELEASE=1` goes ahead of everyday builds in the line. `BUILD_QUEUE_SCRIPT` names the queue and `HUSHGRAM_BUILD_WRAPPER` the script that runs Gradle. Without them the scripts run as they did before and say so.
* The push gate runs its quick checks first. The catalog, both lints and the runtime tests go in one build, and the patch tests (most of a quarter hour) and the bundle come after it, so a lint slip or a stale catalog stops the push in a few minutes. A declared build with no fixture stops it before anything is built.
* The push gate keeps its results when it removes its worktree, pass or fail. The test results, the bundle and its SBOM, each declared build's patch reports and its passing patch run go in a folder named for the commit, under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HushGram\gate` unless `HUSHGRAM_GATE_CACHE` names another place, with a manifest of what the gate ran and how far it got. The newest three are kept. Before, a gate's test results went with its worktree, and the release check had to run the patch tests again.
* `build-release-receipt.ps1 -FromGate` and `validate-release-facts.ps1 -FromGate` read the gate's run of the commit they check instead of doing its work again. The receipt takes the gate's bundle and SBOM when none was built here, and reads each declared build's patch run back when the gate made it with the same bundle, catalog, desktop CLI and APK. The release check takes the gate's test results, bundle and receipt when the checkout has none, and the index push passes `-FromGate` by itself. A run is read only when its manifest, tree, hashes and test counts still hold up for that commit, and every check runs on what's read. Anything else and the scripts build, test and patch as before.
* The index push that follows a release doesn't build and test the release's sources all over again. When every file it pushes is an index file and the only lines changed since a commit the gate passed are the index, the README's latest release sentence and the bug form's version, the gate is skipped. The release switch, the commit checks, the suites and the release check against the published release still run. The gate runs anyway when the kept run doesn't hold up, or when it would patch a build here that the kept run didn't patch with the same fixture and desktop CLI.
* The gate's kept run is held to more before a push or a release leans on it. An index push is gated in full when the fixture folder has changed since the gate ran, since a build added or replaced there changes what the patch tests read. The same goes when `pre-push.ps1` or `gate-evidence.ps1` changed after the run was made, or when a kept patched APK, patch report or merge no longer matches what the gate stamped. Two gates of one commit no longer write into the same folder. The second one stops until the first is done. Pruning still keeps the newest three runs, and failed runs go before passed ones, so a release's passed run survives a busy day of pushes.
* When the fixture folder holds more than one copy of the Instagram version the bundle declares, the gate patches the declared build, picked by its version code. It used to take whichever file sorted first, so a second full bundle kept beside the declared one sent the patch step to the wrong build.
* `scripts/release/` holds the helpers a release used to need by hand. `preflight.ps1` runs the quick checks in a few minutes before the source push (a clean checkout on main, every declared build in the fixture folder, the desktop CLI, the release facts, the CHANGELOG section and the patch tests that read no Instagram build) and says how long each took. `patch-all-builds.ps1` patches every Instagram build in the fixture folder with the whole catalog and reports the patches each applied and missed and the CLI's warnings, patching a build kept as a bundle from the bundle rather than its base split, and reading the gate's run back with `-FromGate`. `release_notes.py` builds the GitHub notes from a CHANGELOG section with every bullet in it, and `count_tests.py` counts the test results, the gate's included, and prints the index description's validation sentence. The release steps in CONTRIBUTING.md use all four.
* A push that changes a PowerShell script has every tracked script parsed before anything else runs, and a script that doesn't parse stops the push. Most of them run only for a release or with a phone, so a slip such as a variable name run into a colon used to surface there first.

## Install or update

* Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer is still all you need.
* Update the HushGram source in Morphe Manager, or add it with the link in the README.
* Coming from 0.0.7, 24 switches start off now where they used to start on. If something you used seems gone after the update, turn its switch back on in HushGram settings.
* Instagram 450.0.0.50.77 is still the target. Build 385611438, the (480-640dpi) bundle on APKMirror, is the one every check runs on. The other arm64 builds (385611395, 385611400, 385611404, 385611431) and the x86 and x86_64 ones (385611439, 385611440) patch too, but Manager still names only 385611438, so it shows the others as unsupported. The .mpp is a patch bundle, not an Instagram APK.
* Keep the manager's signing key for updates, so the new build installs over the old one and you stay signed in.
* Read Before you sign in in the README first. A spare account keeps your main one out of it.

## Validation

2925 runtime tests and all 1213 patch tests passed locally. All 79 patches applied to Instagram 450.0.0.50.77 build 385611438 without forcing, and the resource and injected-code checks passed. The other six builds of 450.0.0.50.77 took all 79 patches too. The receipt and SHA256SUMS.txt beside the bundle list every file's hash.

hushpinterest.title: v0.0.7
hushpinterest.body:
HushPinterest 0.0.7 has 27 patches for Pinterest 14.39.0. It's built on Morphe patcher 1.15.1, so it needs Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer. A patched Pinterest can now sign up for push notifications, which Google's Firebase used to refuse, and you can pick the folder your downloads go to. Hide ads also looks inside the rows of pins on Home and under a pin, and Hide shopping catches store product pins.

This release moves to Pinterest 14.39.0. Patch 14.39.0 and install it over your current HushPinterest with the same signing key, and your settings stay as they are.

## What's new

- Pinterest 14.39.0 is now the supported version. All 27 patches apply to it, and 14.38.0 is no longer a target.
- New Fix push notifications patch, on by default. Google's Firebase service only signs Pinterest up for push notifications when the request names Pinterest's original signature, and a patched Pinterest is signed with a different one, so it never got a notification token. The patch gives Firebase the original signature's fingerprint when Pinterest signs up and changes nothing else in the request. Its switch is on the new Notifications page under More settings.
- Download pins has a new Save in Pinterest's folder switch, and it starts off. With it on, downloads go to Pictures/100PINT/Pins, the folder Pinterest's own image saves use, instead of filling up Download. Board downloads, long-press downloads and retries from Download history follow it too, and the download messages and Download history point to that folder instead of Downloads. (#5)
- Download pins can also save into a folder you pick. Tap Pick a download folder and choose any folder inside Pictures, DCIM, Download or Documents in Android's folder picker. Android's Downloads still does the saving, so nothing gets copied and no storage permission is needed. Each download in Download history remembers its folder, so its messages point there even after you pick another. Tap the row again to pick a different folder or go back to Download. Save in Pinterest's folder wins while it's on, and picking a folder turns it off. (#5)
- Long-press download keeps Pinterest's own buttons again. Holding a pin in a grid showed only Download, because Pinterest's Pin, Share and More ideas buttons never sprang back in after the patch laid the menu out again. Now all three show with Download after them, and letting go on any of them does what it says.
- System share sheet opens Android's share menu from a pin's Share button on 14.39.0. The pin's id is now read from the fields Pinterest's share sheet fills, found when you patch, instead of by a name that pointed somewhere else in 14.39.0, which left Pinterest's own sheet showing with the switch on.
- Hide advertising ID now keeps Pinterest's browser ID out of Google's Block Store too. Pinterest kept it there so that, on a phone with Google backup on, it would outlast an uninstall and come back on a new phone, which let a fresh install send the old ID before you'd signed in. With the switch on, Pinterest finds no saved ID, and when it tries to save one it deletes the stored copy instead, so a reinstall starts fresh. The browser cookie for the install you're using keeps working the way it did.
- The settings home ends with a Support HushPinterest row. Tapping it opens the Ko-fi page in your browser, and if no app can open it you get a message with the address instead. Its text is translated into German, Spanish, Indonesian, Brazilian Portuguese and Turkish.
- Download board no longer saves a board's pins a second time once they've dropped off Download history. The history still shows the newest 32 entries, and it now remembers the 500 before those. Removing a pin from Download history forgets its older downloads too.
- Morphe Manager and the patch index now show the HushPinterest icon next to the source instead of the owner's GitHub picture.
- Hide ads now looks inside modules. A row of ideas on Home or a group of pins under the pin you opened carries its own pins, and an ad in one got through because Hide ads only checked the row itself. Now the ad comes out of the row, and a row left with nothing in it goes too, heading and all. Hide AI-labeled pins and Hide shopping reach inside rows the same way. A pin that carries Pinterest's promotion or campaign ID also counts as an ad now. (#6)
- Hide shopping and product pins now hides a shop's product pins, the ones shown with a store name like Target or Nordstrom Rack and a tag icon under the picture. Pinterest doesn't mark them as paid, so Hide ads keeps leaving them alone, but they slipped past Hide shopping too. With Debug logging on, the diagnostic report also lists the shopping and ad fields of what stays, so a pin that still gets through can be tracked down. (#6)
- Hide ads now catches shopping spotlight stories on the feed models that keep the story kind as Pinterest's own type rather than as text. Before, only the text form counted, so a spotlight on those models stayed unless Hide shopping was on too. Other stories stay put, and Hide shopping still works on its own.
- If a Pinterest update leaves Hide ads only part of its hooks, the Feed page now names the feed lists and ad panels it couldn't reach instead of reading as if everything's covered. The diagnostic report lists every list and panel with how much of it went in, and names the two places no hook reaches yet (Shopping ideas groups in search results and shopping wrappers under related pins). A full build reads the same as before.
- Strip link tracking has a new Plain pin links switch on the Privacy page, and it starts off. With it on, a pin.it link you copy or share becomes the pin's own pinterest.com link, so it doesn't tell Pinterest who shared it. Links Pinterest makes for Copy link or a share change right away, even when you send a pin straight to another app, because HushPinterest sees which pin Pinterest made the link for. Any other short link you copy is checked with Pinterest in the background and swapped on the clipboard a moment later, as long as you haven't copied something else by then. Shared text never waits for that check, and if it fails or takes longer than 4 seconds the short link stays. A pin link from one of Pinterest's country sites, like de.pinterest.com or www.pinterest.co.uk, becomes the same www.pinterest.com link with no lookup, and a pin's sent link drops the invite code that ties it to whoever sent it. Board links and account pages stay as they are, and so does a pin link that still carries a parameter after tracking tags come off.
- HushPinterest settings has a new page under More settings, Pinterest's own settings. It shows where Pinterest keeps its own theme, privacy, notification, AI content and cellular autoplay settings, and names each step through Pinterest's menus in the language Pinterest is using. HushPinterest doesn't change any of them. The AI content row explains how it differs from Hide AI-labeled pins, and the autoplay row says Pinterest may still load part of a video ahead of time.
- HushPinterest drops its Android 9 code now that Pinterest 14.39.0 needs Android 10. The file picker saves go, along with their Pending saves page, and so does the app folder Android 9 used for diagnostic reports. Every download is handed to Android's Downloads, and a selection's summary no longer has a Saved line, since only the picker ever filled it.
- HushPinterest's short messages now show as Pinterest's own toasts. When a dialog is open, a message is long or has more than one line, or the Pinterest build's toast code isn't what the patch expects, they stay Android toasts.

## Behind the scenes

- The release receipt, the patch verifier and the device lease now hold the patched app to Android 10 (API 29), the same floor the settings patch sets since the Android 9 code went. They still expected API 28, so a target whose own floor was below 29 would have failed the receipt.
- While a release hold keeps the published index behind source, the release check now wants the bug report form to name the published release with the Pinterest build it was made for. It used to pair the published version with source's newer build, a combination nobody filing a report would have.
- The privacy doc now follows Pinterest's launch event, which carries the full URL the app was opened with, to both of its uploads: `v3/callback/event/` and `v3/callback/track_funnel/{event}/`. Disable analytics already stops both.
- The privacy doc now lists every header Pinterest puts on its API requests, with where each value comes from and whether a patch covers it. The advertising ID header is the only one a patch changes today.
- The header table now explains the last two. `X-Pinterest-AppState` only says whether the app is in front and online. `X-Pinterest-Platform-BID` is Pinterest's `_b` browser cookie, which the app keeps in Google Block Store (backed up to the cloud when Block Store offers end-to-end encryption), so it can survive a reinstall or a move to a new phone.
- The privacy doc now follows the install ID to all of its uses. Besides its own header it's Pinterest's signed-out ID, AppsFlyer's `unauth_id`, and the ID on analytics, push and reCAPTCHA events. A signed-in emulator kept its session, feed and search after the ID was swapped for a fresh one, so no hook is planned for it.
- System share sheet now checks, when you patch, that Pinterest gives a pin the share kind the patch makes pin links for. A build that numbers its kinds differently is refused instead of sharing a board's id as a pin link. The fixture tests cover that refusal and the two ways the sendable's constructor can stop naming its id and kind.
- Long-press download now checks that a menu button's detach handler really cancels the spring driver the patch clears, by finding the cancel call on that driver, not just a call that reads it. The fixture tests pin 14.39.0's spring fields and refuse a handler without the cancel.
- The patch verifier's System share and long-press checks now match the patch. The sendable's id and kind have to be its own fields written through itself, the springs reset needs a zero that isn't the button's register, and the spring driver has to be one the detach handler cancels.
- `scripts/test-app-inventory.ps1` checks the inventory tool on two tiny real APKs in `scripts/checks/inventory-fixture`, every section and the diff between them, in PowerShell 7 and 5.1. The script contract suite runs it, and `scripts/checks/build-inventory-fixtures.ps1` rebuilds the APKs from their Java sources.
- The Pinterest reference docs now describe 14.39.0. The APK facts, class and method names, endpoints and resource names were checked against the 14.39.0 build, with the old 14.38.0 name kept next to each one that moved. The patch reference covers all 27 patches. The signed-in screen survey and the runtime measurements are still the 14.38.0 runs, and the docs say so.
- The patch reference records the push sign-up check from a fresh emulator install. Without Fix push notifications, Firebase refused the sign-up with a 403. With it, the same install registered with Firebase.
- A fixture run that passes every check is now kept under a key made from the bundle, the APK, the patch selection and the hash of every verifier script, and a later run with the same key reuses it instead of patching Pinterest again. The release push gate patches each declared fixture once and the release receipt reads those runs. `scripts/patch-for-device.ps1` can sign the gate's patched APK for a phone when its key matches. A changed input means a full run, and a failed run is never kept.
- The push gate now runs the unit tests and lint in a quick Gradle pass before the fixture suite, so a broken test stops the push in minutes instead of after the Pinterest APK runs. Each pass waits for its own slot in the build queue.
- The script contract tests now parse every tracked PowerShell file, so a syntax slip in a script that only runs on a release or with a phone shows up on the next script push.
- Releases now run in stages from `scripts/release/release.ps1`: prepare, preflight, gate, build and publish. Each stage checks that the one before it finished, and running one again after it's done changes nothing. The CHANGELOG cut refuses any bullet that isn't a one-line Pinterest or Tooling entry and names it. The GitHub notes carry every bullet of the section. `publish-release.ps1` pushes the index commit as soon as the release is up and ends with `verify-published-index.ps1`. The notes and index text come from `release_text.py`, which has its own unit tests. (#3)
- `scripts/app-inventory.ps1` lists what a Pinterest build talks to and what it reads about the device. That covers its Retrofit endpoints with their verbs, the startup tasks, the hosts its code names, who opens connections, the SDK packages, and who reads the advertising ID, Android ID, install referrer or device identifiers. The lines come out sorted, with renamed packages written as `~`, so `-BaseApk` can diff two builds. The [privacy notes](docs/pinterest-14.39.0-privacy.md) now carry the 14.39.0 inventory and what changed from 14.38.0.

## Reported issues

Where each report on the tracker stands with this release.

- #6, ads getting through (@darenrue). Hide ads now checks inside the rows of pins on Home and under a pin you open, where an ad could slip past before. The store cards with a shop name and a tag icon, like the Target one in the report, aren't paid ads, so Hide ads leaves them. `Hide shopping and product pins` now hides them, and it starts off, so turn it on under Feed. The issue stays open until it's confirmed on your phone.
- #5, save downloads to a folder you choose (@boox3). New here. `Pick a download folder` under Pin actions saves pins straight into any folder in Pictures, DCIM, Download or Documents. `Save in Pinterest's folder` puts them in Pictures/100PINT/Pins with Pinterest's own saves.
- #4, one patch source for every Hush app (@Stark-0505). Still open. HushPinterest is still its own source in this release.
- #3, matching the Morphe template's release setup (@Stark-0505). Partly in. The patch index now goes up in the same step as the release, so Morphe Manager offers the update as soon as it's out, and a check after every release confirms the index matches. Moving to the template's own release workflow is still open.
- #2, Download pin said Pinterest had no original image (@Stark-0505). Fixed in 0.0.5. Download pin gets the original image behind the size Pinterest shows.

## Install

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 1.34.0 or newer.
2. Add HushPinterest as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushPinterest
3. Download Pinterest **14.39.0**, version code **14398020**, as the universal APK, and patch it. It needs Android 10 or newer.
4. Uninstall the stock Pinterest first, since Android won't put one over the other. Save anything you keep only on the phone before you do. Your boards and pins come back when you sign in.
5. Sign in with your email and a Pinterest password. If you joined through Google or Facebook, tap **Forgot your password?** on Pinterest's login page to set one first.
6. Right after your first patch, export Morphe Manager's signing key (Settings, then System, then Import & export, then Signing key) and keep it somewhere private. Updates only install over a Pinterest signed with that same key.

Already on HushPinterest? Skip steps 4 and 5. Patch 14.39.0 with the same key and install it over the one you have.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Pinterest APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushPinterest#install). `SHA256SUMS.txt` is signed with the HushPinterest release key, fingerprint `FCE5 ECE3 182A 647B 3AF2  C5ED 2DC3 5E8D 5C00 E8A6`. [How to check a download](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushPinterest#verify-a-release-download).

## Validation

All 204 patch tests and 702 extension tests passed on this commit, none skipped. The bundle attached here was patched onto a real Pinterest 14.39.0 APK with Morphe's desktop patcher, and all 27 patches applied without forcing. `release-receipt-0.0.7.json` records that result, the APK's hash and what patching changed in the app's manifest. Pick a download folder, the store pin filter and the module filter for Hide ads were also checked on a phone running this build's patches.

hushtelegram.title: v0.0.12
hushtelegram.body:
HushTelegram v0.0.12 has 56 patches for telegram.org's Telegram 12.10.6 (`org.telegram.messenger.web`) and the official Telegram beta 12.10.7 (`org.telegram.messenger.beta`). Fifty-four are selected by default, and the one new switch starts off. Most of this release is about reading easier. Every patch description, settings row and message inside HushTelegram is rewritten in plain English, and Expert mode groups the patches the way you'd look for them. Keep deleted messages now marks a message the moment it's deleted while the chat is open, and it can clear what it kept. On the beta, Disable analytics also stops Firebase's crash and session reports.

## What's new

* **Telegram:** On Telegram Beta, Disable analytics now also turns off Firebase's crash and session reports. Telegram's own crash reporter setup, which handed Crashlytics your user ID and username and switched collection back on at every launch, no longer runs, and Crashlytics' own setting is saved off, so it stops collecting and sending from the next start. Session reports stop right away. Push notifications don't change, and the regular build has neither reporter. Turning the switch off brings both back at the next launch.
* **Telegram:** A new Turn off beta debug logs switch, off by default, stops Telegram Beta from writing debug logs all the time. The beta turned them on at every start, its connection log included, and its own debug menu couldn't stop that. Logs already saved stay until you clear them, and the regular build doesn't change. Restart Telegram after you turn it on.
* **Telegram:** Keep deleted messages has a new Clear kept messages row in HushTelegram settings, right under its switch. One tap gives every message it kept, in every signed-in account, to Telegram's own deletion, so they go the way they would have without the patch. A notice tells you how many went. It's translated into all five languages.
* **Telegram:** Keep deleted messages now marks a message as deleted the moment someone deletes it while you have that chat open. Before, the label only showed up after you left the chat and came back.
* **Telegram:** Contributors have a new audit of the stock beta, signed in on a real phone. It covers a live search ad, the app's own settings screens, what the app sends on the local network, and how busy it stays in the foreground and background. It also separates contact sync from contact suggestions and notes what you can't learn from encrypted traffic.
* **Telegram:** Added an app audit for sponsored-message delivery, ad reporting, telemetry, contact sync and current patch opportunities on the pinned 12.10.6 APK.
* **Telegram:** Build and Pause reports now use Morphe Manager's patch names for haptic feedback and link tracking. The pause card's test now matches its current wording about Debug logging.
* **Telegram:** Contributors now have a factory-app reference for the pinned APK, with the first-run flow, manifest entry points, stable anchors and fixture-update steps.
* **Telegram:** The three patch options (your Telegram API ID and hash, and your Google Maps key) have clearer names and say where to find each value.
* **Telegram:** Messages inside HushTelegram are plainer too: the notification status lines, the pause and safe mode notes, update check results, settings file errors, and the "this build doesn't change" notes now say what happened and what to do next, with no technical words. All five languages are updated.
* **Telegram:** The rows in HushTelegram settings now say in plain English what you'll notice when a switch is on, and a few titles are clearer (Stop vibrations on taps, Remove link tracking tags, Show where a profile photo is stored). The translations are updated to match.
* **Telegram:** Every patch description in Morphe Manager is rewritten in plain English. Each one now says what changes on screen, why you might want it, and ends with where to find its switch in HushTelegram settings and whether it starts on or off.
* **Telegram:** Each patch's description in Morphe Manager now says which page of HushTelegram settings holds its switch, under the switch's own name when that differs, and whether it starts on or off. Nothing is hidden behind Expert mode: every patch but the two credential patches was already in the default selection, and the README's install steps now say so.
* **Telegram:** Expert mode's Chats group held 41 of the 55 patches. It's now split into groups you'd look in: Chats for the chat list, Conversations for inside a chat, Playback, Notifications, Theme, Interface, Stories and Search. Hide promotional banners and Hide Premium, gifts and Stars moved to Ads, and Disable update checks moved to Updates.
* **Telegram:** Strip link tracking's description now reads plainly. It still removes only the listed tracking keys and still starts off.

### Tooling

* **Tooling:** The scripts that patch Telegram with the desktop CLI (the all-patches check, the release receipt and the selection matrix) now wait their turn in the build queue that `BUILD_QUEUE_SCRIPT` names, so they don't fight a Gradle build for the same cores. Release runs go to the front. Without a queue they run straight away and print a warning.
* **Tooling:** The pre-push hook now reads `HUSHTELEGRAM_BUILD_WRAPPER` and its other settings from your user environment when the shell has them empty, not only when they're missing, since pwsh keeps an empty variable around. With no wrapper at all, its own `gradlew` run waits in the build queue too.
* **Tooling:** The selection matrix reads the whole fixture APK for its hash twice a run, before the first case and after the last, instead of up to three times in each of its 74 cases. Each case still checks the APK's size and write time, and a changed APK still fails the run.
* **Tooling:** The patch tests that open the vendor Telegram APKs now run in their own Gradle task, `:patches:fixtureTest`. `:patches:test` still runs every patch test and passes `--tests` on to it, while `:patches:test -x :patches:fixtureTest` runs the rest without opening an APK. The release check counts the results from both folders.
* **Tooling:** The pre-push gate runs its cheap checks before the long fixture suite. After the script suites it checks the release facts right away when no code changed, then runs every Gradle task except the fixture tests, the advisory scan and the facts that read the runtime results, and only then the fixture tests. A broken script, lint error or stale fact now stops a push before any vendor APK is patched.
* **Tooling:** `verify-all-patches.ps1 -KeepIn <dir>` keeps a clean run's patched APK and CLI report, stamped with the commit and the hashes of the fixture, bundle, patch list and CLI. `build-release-receipt.ps1 -AppliedDir <dir>` reads a kept run whose stamp matches instead of patching that fixture a second time, and still runs every check on it. Anything that doesn't match gets patched as before.
* **Tooling:** Releases now run from `scripts/release/release.ps1`, one command per stage: prepare, preflight, build, publish and index. Each stage records the commit it finished on and won't start until the one before it has finished. A stage can be run again after a fix, and one that already finished checks its work and says so. Preflight is a five-minute check of the scripts, release text, facts and the patch tests without the fixture suite. Build runs the full tests, the bundle and every declared Telegram build once, and the receipt reads those runs. The release notes builder now lives in the repo too, and it carries every bullet of the version's CHANGELOG section and checks the published notes still do.

## Install

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 1.34.0 or newer.
2. Add HushTelegram as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushTelegram
3. Get Telegram **12.10.6**, version code 71129, from [APKMirror's Telegram (Web version) page](https://www.apkmirror.com/apk/telegram-fz-llc/telegram-web-version/telegram-web-version-12-10-6-release/) and pick the universal APK. It's telegram.org's own build. The Download button on telegram.org now gives you 13.0.0, so use the APKMirror link for this release. If you already have the official beta 12.10.7, build 71239, you can patch that instead. The patched app needs Android 9 or newer.
4. Coming from v0.0.11? Patch again and install over it with the same Morphe Manager signing key. New to HushTelegram? Uninstall the stock Telegram first, since Android won't put one over the other. Your chats come back when you sign in, but secret chats don't. Back up Morphe Manager's signing key after your first patch. You'll need it for every update.
5. If Telegram won't send you a login code, register your own app at [my.telegram.org/apps](https://my.telegram.org/apps). Use only letters and numbers in the short name. Then select **Use registered Telegram API credentials**, fill in `apiId` and `apiHash`, and patch again. The result installs over your current HushTelegram build. Keep both values private.
6. For notifications, open Telegram's Settings, then Notifications and Sounds, and turn on Keep-Alive Service and Background Connection.
7. To change HushTelegram's switches, open Telegram's Settings and tap HushTelegram settings.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Telegram APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushTelegram#install).

## Validation

786 runtime tests and 364 patch tests passed locally, along with both Android lints. All 56 patches applied without forcing to Telegram 12.10.6 and to the 12.10.7 beta, build 71239. The release receipt checked each patched app's manifest, native libraries, resources and alignment.

hushthreads.title: v0.0.12
hushthreads.body:
HushThreads v0.0.12 has 17 patches for Threads 450.0.0.51.78 (`com.instagram.barcelona`), and it works with Threads 449.0.0.54.82 and 448.0.0.54.85 too. It's built on Morphe patcher 1.15.1, so you need Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer.

Six patches are new in this one, Save photos and videos, Max image quality, Disable screenshot detection, Change version code, Remove share targets and Trust user-added certificates. HushThreads also has its own row in Threads' settings now, and Hide ads catches more of the ad units in your feed.

## Threads

- New Trust user-added certificates patch, not selected by default. Threads accepts certificates you've installed on your phone yourself, such as one a work network needs or a debugging proxy's, wherever it relies on Android's own certificate checks. Threads' network code checks Meta's certificates on its own as well and this patch doesn't change that, so a proxy still can't read most of Threads' traffic to Meta. HushThreads settings list it under Set when you patched.
- New Remove share targets patch, not selected by default. Threads stops showing up in the share sheet other apps open, so it isn't offered when you share a link, a photo or a video from somewhere else. The patch takes Threads' share entries out of its manifest, and any direct share contacts Threads might list there go too. Sharing from Threads to other apps still works. HushThreads settings list it under Set when you patched.
- New Change version code patch, not selected by default. It raises the patched Threads' version code to the highest Android allows, so Google Play stops offering Meta's updates over it. Every build with the patch has that same code, so an older Threads patched with it installs over a newer one too. Threads' own checks of its version code, at start and in its job scheduler, still see the code Meta built. Going back to stock Threads afterwards means uninstalling first, which deletes Threads' data, and later HushThreads builds need the patch too.
- Hide ads now also takes out the feed units Threads itself marks as ads by their unit type, even when the post inside doesn't carry the ad flag. That covers plain ads, ads for ads, the two kinds of ad pivot and the ads feedback prompts. Suggested accounts and other recommendation units stay, and so do ordinary posts. The Hide ads switch covers both checks.
- New Max image quality patch, off by default in Manager. Threads gets every photo in several sizes and normally loads the one closest to your screen's width. With this on it loads the largest size it has, so photos look sharper and each one is a bigger download. Square crops stay square and nothing changes size on screen. The switch is under Feed in HushThreads settings as Full size photos, and turning it off or pausing HushThreads gives Threads its own choice back.
- New Disable screenshot detection patch, off by default in Manager. Threads isn't told when you take a screenshot. It stops looking through your photos for new screenshots, and on Android 14 and newer it doesn't ask Android to report screenshots of the feed. Your screenshots are still saved. The switch sits in HushThreads' Privacy settings, and turning it off or pausing HushThreads gives Threads its own behavior back.
- Restore screens on re-signed builds now also covers FBNS, the push service Meta's apps share. FBNS checks the app's own signing certificate before it hands it pushes, and on a re-signed build it now gets Threads' original certificate there too, the same way Threads' other security checks already did. Refs #6.
- New Save photos and videos patch, selected by default. A post's menu gets a Save row right under Copy link, with Threads' own download icon. It reads Save photo, Save video or Save all, depending on what the post holds, and posts without a photo or video don't get it. A tap saves to your gallery, photos to Pictures/Threads and videos to Movies/Threads with their sound, at the best size Threads has. A carousel saves every page in order, photos and videos alike, and its files carry the post's id so two posts never mix. The menu closes once the save starts, as it does after Copy link. A new Downloads page in HushThreads settings has the switch plus quality, folder and file name options, and it shows how the last carousel save went. Pause takes the row away too.
- HushThreads now has its own row in Threads' settings, right above More settings, so you can open it from your profile's settings like any other page. It's drawn the way Threads draws its own rows. It grows with large text, and TalkBack reads it out and opens it with a double tap. The launcher shortcut and Additional settings on the App info page still work.
- HushThreads now patches Threads 450.0.0.51.78 (version code 512008342, the 240-480dpi build) as well as 449 and 448. Threads 450 rearranged the code behind three patches. Disable video autoplay now finds the flag PostVideo plays by from the check that sets the player going, Block background-return feed refresh follows the warm-start check's new branch and the second server setting 450 can read its time limit from, and Pure black dark mode also looks in the helper where 450 builds its dark colors.
